items.prompt:
Text A: 'Frogs are amphibians that live near ponds. They have smooth, wet skin and long back legs for jumping.'
Text B: 'Frogs eat insects like flies and mosquitoes. They catch insects with their long, sticky tongues.'

What do both texts tell you? What unique idea does each text add?
items.answer: Both texts are about frogs. Text A adds the unique idea about frogs being amphibians with specific body features (skin and legs). Text B adds the unique idea about what frogs eat and how they hunt using their sticky tongues.

steps: Both texts describe frogs.
Text A adds: amphibian, smooth wet skin, long back legs for jumping (body and habitat).
Text B adds: eats insects, catches them with a long sticky tongue (diet and hunting method).
Shared: both describe frogs as living things with interesting characteristics.
Unique to each: Text A covers body structure; Text B covers feeding behavior.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Honey is made by bees. Worker bees collect nectar from flowers and bring it back to the hive.'
Text B: 'Honey has been used for thousands of years. People use it to sweeten food and as a medicine.'

If you wanted to know how honey is made, which text would you use? If you wanted to know how people use honey, which text would you use? Explain.
items.answer: To learn how honey is made, I would use Text A because it describes bees collecting nectar and bringing it to the hive. To learn how people use honey, I would use Text B because it talks about honey being used as a sweetener and medicine.

steps: Text A explains the process: bees collect nectar and bring it to the hive.
Text B explains human uses: sweetening food and medicine.
'How is honey made?' matches Text A.
'How do people use honey?' matches Text B.
Each text answers a different question about the same topic.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Volcanoes are mountains that can erupt. Hot melted rock called lava flows out from the top.'
Text B: 'Volcanoes can be very dangerous. Ash and lava can destroy towns nearby. But lava rock creates new land over time.'

Both texts mention lava. What does each text say about lava that the other does not?
items.answer: Text A says lava is hot melted rock that flows out from the top of the volcano. Text B says lava can destroy towns but also creates new land over time. Text A focuses on what lava is; Text B focuses on what lava does.

steps: Text A on lava: hot melted rock, flows out from the top.
Text B on lava: destroys towns, creates new land over time.
What does only Text A say about lava? That it is hot melted rock and how it exits.
What does only Text B say about lava? Its destructive and constructive effects.
Both mention lava but from different perspectives: what it is vs. what it does.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Trees provide oxygen for us to breathe. Their roots hold soil in place and prevent floods.'
Text B: 'Trees provide homes for birds and squirrels. Many animals depend on trees for food, like nuts and berries.'

How are the two texts similar in their main message? How are they different?
items.answer: Both texts share the main message that trees are very important. But they are different: Text A focuses on how trees help the environment (oxygen, soil, preventing floods), while Text B focuses on how trees help animals (homes and food).

steps: Main message of Text A: trees help the environment and humans.
Main message of Text B: trees help animals.
Similarity: both show that trees are important to living things.
Difference: Text A is about environmental and human benefits; Text B is about animal benefits.
Same big idea (trees are important), different audience (humans/environment vs. animals).

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Astronauts train for years before going to space. They practice floating in big pools of water to get ready for zero gravity.'
Text B: 'In space, astronauts float because there is very little gravity. They must be careful so tools do not float away.'

Both texts mention floating. What is the connection between the floating in Text A and the floating in Text B?
items.answer: Text A explains that astronauts practice floating in pools to prepare for zero gravity in space. Text B explains what floating in space is actually like. The floating in Text A (training in pools) prepares astronauts for the floating in Text B (real life in space). They are connected: the pool practice gets astronauts ready for the real experience.

steps: Text A: astronauts practice floating in pools to prepare for zero gravity.
Text B: in space, astronauts float because of little gravity.
Connection: the pool training in Text A is practice for the real floating in Text B.
Text A shows preparation; Text B shows the real situation.
They connect because the pool floating mimics the space floating.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Wolves live and hunt in groups called packs. The pack works together to catch large animals.'
Text B: 'Wolves are important to ecosystems. When wolf populations were removed from Yellowstone Park, deer ate too many plants and the rivers changed.'

Text A describes how wolves behave. Text B describes why wolves matter. Using both texts, explain why a wolf pack working together connects to the ecosystem idea in Text B.
items.answer: Text A shows that wolves hunt in packs, which makes them effective predators of large animals. Text B shows that without wolves, deer (large animals) ate too many plants, causing damage. The connection is: the pack hunting in Text A is why wolves can control deer populations, which is the key reason they matter to ecosystems in Text B.

steps: Text A: wolves hunt together and catch large animals.
Text B: without wolves, deer overate plants and damaged rivers.
Connection: wolves catching large animals (Text A) = wolves keeping deer in check (Text B).
Pack hunting enables wolf packs to hunt deer effectively.
Effective deer hunting is why wolves matter to the ecosystem.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Water evaporates from oceans and lakes, rises into the sky, and forms clouds.'
Text B: 'Clouds release rain and snow, which flows into rivers and back to the ocean.'

These two texts describe two parts of the same process. What is the process? How do the two texts fit together?
items.answer: The process is the water cycle. Text A describes the first half: water evaporating and forming clouds. Text B describes the second half: clouds releasing rain and snow that flows back to the ocean. Together, the two texts describe the complete water cycle from beginning to end.

steps: Text A: evaporation and cloud formation.
Text B: rain and snow falling, flowing back to ocean.
What process does this describe? The water cycle.
Text A = first half (up): water rises and forms clouds.
Text B = second half (down): water falls and returns to the ocean.
Together they form the complete cycle.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Polar bears have thick white fur to stay warm. Their large paws help them swim long distances.'
Text B: 'Polar bears are endangered. Climate change is melting the sea ice they live on, leaving them with less habitat.'

What does Text A tell you about how polar bears are adapted? What does Text B tell you is threatening those adaptations?
items.answer: Text A tells us that polar bears are adapted to cold environments with thick fur for warmth and large paws for swimming on sea ice. Text B tells us that climate change is melting the sea ice, which threatens those adaptations because the ice habitat they depend on is disappearing.

steps: Text A: thick fur = stay warm. Large paws = swim. Both adaptations are for cold, icy environments.
Text B: climate change melts sea ice. Less habitat.
How does Text B threaten Text A's adaptations?
If sea ice melts, there is less ice for polar bears to swim between.
Their adaptations are for ice; without ice, the adaptations cannot help them.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'The library has books, magazines, and computers for people to use for free.'
Text B: 'Libraries hold events like story time, coding clubs, and art classes for the whole community.'

A student says: 'Both texts are saying the same thing: libraries are good.' Is this too simple? What do the texts add beyond just saying libraries are good?
items.answer: The student is too simple. Text A specifically describes what resources the library has (books, magazines, computers, free access). Text B specifically describes what activities the library offers (story time, coding clubs, art). Together they show two different ways libraries serve the community: resources and programs. Just saying 'libraries are good' misses these specific details.

steps: Text A: books, magazines, computers, free. Specific resources.
Text B: story time, coding clubs, art classes. Specific programs.
The student says both say 'libraries are good.' Is that the full picture?
No: Text A tells you WHAT resources are available.
Text B tells you WHAT activities happen there.
These are two specific, different things libraries do. The student's summary is too vague.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles from Canada to Mexico every fall. They fly together in large groups.'
Text B: 'Monarch butterflies are orange and black. Their bright colors warn birds that they taste bad.'

Using both texts, describe a monarch butterfly as completely as you can.
items.answer: A monarch butterfly is orange and black. Its bright colors warn birds that it tastes bad, so they leave it alone. Each fall, monarchs migrate thousands of miles from Canada to Mexico, flying together in large groups.

steps: From Text B: orange and black, bright colors warn birds.
From Text A: migrates from Canada to Mexico in fall, flies in large groups.
Combine both to get a complete description.
Appearance from Text B + migration behavior from Text A = full picture.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Soil is made of tiny bits of rock, dead plants, and living things like worms. It takes hundreds of years to form.'
Text B: 'Healthy soil is important for growing food. When soil loses its nutrients, crops do not grow well.'

What does Text A explain? What does Text B explain? How do both texts together give a more complete understanding of soil?
items.answer: Text A explains what soil is made of and how long it takes to form. Text B explains why healthy soil matters for food production. Together they show that soil is both valuable (Text A: takes hundreds of years to form) and essential (Text B: needed for crops to grow).

steps: Text A: composition of soil (rock bits, dead plants, worms) and how long it takes to form.
Text B: importance of soil for growing food, what happens when nutrients are lost.
Together: Text A shows how rare and slow-forming soil is; Text B shows why that matters.
Combining both: soil is precious (takes long to form) and critical (needed for food).

items.prompt:
Text A: 'The Amazon River is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows through the South American rain forest.'
Text B: 'The Amazon River is home to thousands of species of fish and river dolphins. Many communities along its banks depend on it for water and food.'

Compare what each text focuses on about the Amazon River.
items.answer: Text A focuses on the physical facts about the river: its length and location in South America. Text B focuses on the life and people connected to the river: the animals that live in it and the communities that depend on it. Text A tells us WHAT the river is; Text B tells us WHY it matters.

steps: Text A: length (one of longest), location (South American rain forest).
Text B: fish and dolphins, communities depend on it for water and food.
Text A is about physical geography: what and where.
Text B is about living things and human value: who depends on it.
Same river, two different angles: physical facts vs. biological and human significance.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Hurricanes form over warm ocean water. They have strong winds that spin in a circle.'
Text B: 'Hurricanes can cause heavy rain and floods. People who live near the coast must sometimes leave their homes to stay safe.'

Both texts are about hurricanes. How would you describe a hurricane using information from BOTH texts combined?
items.answer: A hurricane is a powerful storm that forms over warm ocean water. It has strong spinning winds and causes heavy rain and floods. Hurricanes can be so dangerous that people near the coast have to leave their homes.

steps: From Text A: forms over warm water, strong winds that spin.
From Text B: heavy rain, floods, people must evacuate.
Combine: origin + structure + effects + human response.
A complete description uses details from both texts.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Grasshoppers have long back legs for jumping. They can jump 20 times their own body length.'
Text B: 'Grasshoppers make sounds by rubbing their back legs against their wings. This sound is called stridulation.'

Both texts mention grasshoppers' back legs. How are the two uses of the legs described differently?
items.answer: Text A says grasshoppers use their long back legs for jumping, and they can jump 20 times their body length. Text B says grasshoppers rub their back legs against their wings to make sound (stridulation). The same legs serve two different purposes: jumping (Text A) and making sound (Text B).

steps: Text A: back legs = used for jumping (20 times body length).
Text B: back legs = used for making sound by rubbing against wings.
Both mention the same legs but describe different functions.
The key comparison: one leg use is for movement, the other is for communication.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'The Great Wall of China was built to keep out invaders. It stretches for thousands of miles.'
Text B: 'The Great Wall of China is one of the most visited places in the world. Millions of tourists come to see it every year.'

Text A is about the wall's original purpose. Text B is about the wall today. How have the wall's uses changed, based on both texts?
items.answer: Originally, the Great Wall was built as a defense to keep out invaders (Text A). Today, it is no longer used for military defense but is one of the world's most visited tourist sites (Text B). The wall went from a military structure to a historical and cultural attraction.

steps: Text A: original purpose = defense against invaders.
Text B: current purpose = tourism, visited by millions.
The wall's use changed over time: military to cultural.
Together the texts show a before and after: what it was built for and what it is used for now.
